naming_conventions: Every phrase is lowercase ASCII words separated by single spaces.
Heads that differ only in capitalization are DIFFERENT heads in the
skeleton (render_skeleton prints the head verbatim), so they need
different phrases: the lower-case spelling takes the plain phrase, an
ALL-CAPS spelling takes `the capital ...`, a Title-case spelling takes
`the titled ...`. Affected pairs: exp/EXP, d/D, compose/COMPOSE,
concat/CONCAT, cos/COS, sin/SIN, tan/TAN, log/LOG, sqrt/SQRT, sum/SUM,
Single-letter and trailing-underscore heads are the corpus's own opaque
applied variables; they are spelled out as letter names (`eff`, `dee`,
letter names are not numeral words and stay inside L2.
MOD is `the modifier application of`, not `reduced modulo`: this repo's
MOD is modifier application MOD(base, modifier), declared as such in
purpose: The trusted half of the two-stage realization gate (design §3). Each row
maps one template TOKEN -- an operator glyph, a relation, a grouping mark
or a call head -- to one English word phrase. Forward it lexicalizes;
reversed it de-lexicalizes. It is not an independent check and is not
claimed as one: its correctness is carried by review, exactly as
scripts/prose.py's banks are. The independent check is stage 2, the
reading_rules: LONGEST MATCH: reading a surface left to right, take the longest phrase
in this table that matches the upcoming words; if none matches, expect a
numeral run (scripts/numeral_words). The loader makes longest match the
UNIQUE match by enforcing two properties, so the inverter needs no
lookahead policy of its own:
L1 prefix-free -- no phrase is a proper word-prefix of another phrase;
L2 numeral-disjoint -- no phrase word is a word the registered numeral
pair can emit, so one word decides numeral-run versus phrase and a
numeral run may be scanned greedily.
SLOT MARKER: the word `variable` is followed by a numeral run giving the
slot's index; the pair emits the token V<index>. Slot identity is erased
by match_signatures.render_skeleton (slots become position-indexed
placeholders numbered by first occurrence), so index naming is a
skeleton-faithful bijection and the source's own identifiers are carried
in the receipt's `parameters.slot_names` rather than in the gated surface
-- emitting them would be surface outside this table, which R2 forbids.
BRACKET HEADS: a head spelled `X[]` emits the token `X` and takes its
arguments between the `[` and `]` structural rows; the trailing marker is
grammar, not name (match_signatures.lint_stem says the same).

GLYPHS `-` AND `/`: they have no rows of their own. canonicalize() has already rewritten every binary `-` into `+ neg(.)` and every `/` into `* inv(.)`, so the canonical term only ever needs `neg` and `inv`, and a second row spelling the same glyph would break R2b injectivity. Those two rows are keyed by the NODE name and emit the GLYPH, which is what `operator_tokens` below states: a row that emitted the literal token `neg` would re-parse as a call head and the sentence would be fluent and wrong.

BIG OPERATORS: the prefix form `sum_i EXPR` is never emitted. `sum(EXPR)`
parses to the identical node ('call', 'sum', (EXPR,)), so the ordinary
call form covers the head with no extra grammar.
RELATION `~`: deliberately absent. match_signatures.TOKEN_RE has no
alternative for `~`, so no token stream can contain it and a row for it
would be unreachable surface.
